items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Found his medication prescription, and, oh, is this his notebook?
She pulls a crumpled piece of paper from her pocket.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Ha, just as expected, boss. This motel ain't what it seems to be. Ain't no way that letter was written by Stefen.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Take a look. The writing in this letter is delicate and slender, while the writing in this notebook is total chicken scratch. Even a blind person could tell they're written by two different people.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Stefen didn't write the letter. So it's very likely that the person who sent it wasn't Stefen either.
The maid suddenly comes to mind.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: And this ...
She picks up a stack of bound papers from the table.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Ugh, I hate numbers.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I'll leave this one to you, boss.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It appears to be Mr. Stefen's records of his daily expenses, along with some notes.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Cigarettes, alcohol, and a significant amount of psychiatric medication.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It says he was tormented by his hallucinations day after day, so he had to increase his dosage.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hm. And it says he saw a room numbered 707 here.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: The motel only has two floors. There can't be a room starting with seven. Did he describe it at all?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He said the room had a bright red door that seemed completely out of place.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Maybe it was just one of his hallucinations.
There's a flash of red in the hallway.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, it's not that.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He also saw all kinds of things: a pair of twins in the hallway, long hair hanging from the ceiling, and ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He saw Barbara but assumed she was another hallucination.
A small sheep's head is sketched on the paper.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This proves that Barbara's been to the motel.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Which means ...

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Well, I'm sorry to say that I've never met an arcanist with the head of a sheep.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I can help you ask around if you—

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Why did she lie to me?
Argus interrupts her thoughts.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: So, did you find anything useful from the expense record?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I need to talk to the maid.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Hold your horses. We haven't searched the washroom yet.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: You should never skip the bathroom. Ain't you seen the Godfather? Michael Corleone grabs his gun from behind a toilet tank.
She pushes open the bathroom door as she speaks.
Washroom, Tuesday's Motel
The bathroom mirror is surrounded by half-burned candles.
She holds out a hand to signal a stop.
She moves closer and knocks on the mirror. The copper frame gives a hollow echo.
A vivid, venomous green flashes across the mirror, and an ivory face appears in its reflection.
Argus, Argus. You've come to me.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do you know her?
Argus doesn't respond. Her eyes are locked on the mirror, as if lost in a daze.
Argus ...
Argus ... Argus ...
The faint voice echoes around the bathroom, like waves crashing repeatedly against the shore.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: It-It's not possible.
Argus's silence gives rise to a bold speculation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is that Kayla?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: No, there's no way that's her. If you knew Kayla like I do, you'd say the same. This distorted reflection in the mirror is probably a result of the excessive arcanum in this motel.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: A ritual similar to Bloody Mary used to be quite popular among the kids in this town.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: If you look into a mirror at exactly midnight, the spirit within will morph into the shape of the person you desire most. But if you respond to the spirit's call, it will drain your soul from your body.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I always thought those were just myths.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: So did I. But after all the strange things I've seen, I've become less surprised.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: These spirits feed on the energy of our souls. That's why you should never trust a word they say.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: The people who are tricked by them fall into a kind of trance, and, some, like Mr. Stefen, go crazy.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I wonder what he saw in the mirror.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Anyway, I won't repeat his mistake.
She raises her shotgun, ready to fire.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: For mercs like me, the deepest despair ain't external danger; it's internal hesitation.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: If some pale imitation makes me hesitate so easily, then how can I claim to be able to protect others? You've gotta be able to stand your ground.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: A cunning criminal would use every excuse to defend themselves in court. And a scheming spy would wear all kinds of disguises to gather information on the enemy.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: That's why we've gotta stay sharp. When it comes down to it, we only have our own two legs to stand on.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Mercs ain't philosophers. Once a merc starts pondering morals, justice, and ethics, they're digging their own grave.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: For a merc, the mission objective is the only thing that matters. Overthinking don't bring nothing but disaster and destruction.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: That's why she—no, it—won't fool me.
Her gaze is steady.
Memories flash by, distant and playful.
Laughing and running in those grassy fields.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: The folks on the ranch adored little Kayla.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: She was the apple of all their eyes.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: How dare this ugly imitation!
She forcefully loads the shotgun.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: So ...
She aims her gun squarely at the mirror.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Here's my response.
Urgh, i-it hurts.
Argus, Argus. You've come to me.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Let this serve as a reminder to remain vigilant. If there were a "Deceitful Spirit of the Year" award, I'm sure that would win.
